rules.why: A backlog-exhaustion flood leaves connections half-open: the TCP state stays SYN-received, so serror_rate approaches 1 while the connection count to one host exceeds 100.
One host touched across many different services (diff_srv_rate >= 0.55) with a long connection history but few repeats of any single service is port enumeration, not normal client behaviour.
Closed ports answer with RST. A source whose connections are rejected at least 60% of the time is enumerating rather than using services.

true_positive.narrative: (other, state s0) flagged CRITICAL as dos with confidence 1.00. Rule R01 (TCP SYN flood) matched: A backlog-exhaustion flood leaves connections half-open: the TCP state stays SYN-received, so serror_rate approaches 1 while the connection count to one host exceeds 100. Observed: flag=s0, serror_rate=0.090, srv_serror_rate=1, count=486, dst_host_serror_rate=0.070. A further 2 rule(s) also matched. The supervised model assigns 100.0% to 'probe'. Largest contributions: dst_host_diff_srv_rate=1 (raises probe by 0.148); serror_rate=0.09 (raises probe by 0.101); service_entropy_proxy=1 (raises probe by 0.089). The anomaly layer scores this more unusual than 100.0% of benign training traffic. Most isolating features: conn_per_second=486 (+8.6 SD from the benign mean); dst_host_srv_count=1 (-2.0 SD from the benign mean); dst_host_diff_srv_rate=1 (+7.5 SD from the benign mean). Corroboration: 3 of 3 layers agree (signature, supervised, anomaly).
